justifications.c1: Insurer claims data gives per-incident figures (Zurich average £15,000 and an £84,000 garage claim, search-confirmed but dated 2022; Allianz home average £50k via Post), but all are household claims; no £ loss for a commercial hub or e-bike warehouse fire was found (Voi fire has no £ value).
justifications.c2: LFB recorded 206 e-bike/e-scooter fires in London in 2025 (search-confirmed), mostly in homes, and Aviva's 501-business survey shows 54% had a battery incident (13% fires, search-confirmed); these are aggregate rates with no per-hub frequency and no mandated recurring check.
justifications.c3: Paid workarounds are priced: fire-rated charging cabinets at £1,876–£4,430 (UK list prices), plus on-site charging bans (Royal Mail) and supervised-charging advice from Aviva and AXA; a sensor would complement rather than replace a cabinet.
justifications.c4: Only guidance: RRO 2005 general duty with LFB GN103 stating it 'does not create new legal obligations', Aviva Loss Prevention Standards/checklists and RISCAuthority RC61; no sighted policy condition requiring monitoring, and a US broker says wordings have not changed.
justifications.c5: No job advert or budget holder was found; the target buyers are small and financially fragile (Zedify and Pedal Me administrations, ~8 vehicles per Zedify depot), and the large operator (Royal Mail) simply bans charging.
justifications.c6: PowerShelter already bundles BatteryIQ monitoring into charging lockers (NL/North America, trade press), and fire risk assessors and insurer surveyors visit sites, but there is no evidence the latter sell monitoring or that a UK channel does.
justifications.c7: Comparable products exist (Honeywell Li-ion Tamer, quote-only and aimed at BESS; PowerShelter+BatteryIQ; Nomoto startup) but no prices or customer counts; the hub-specific gap is asserted after a limited search.
justifications.c8: Off-gas sensing needs mains power (~275 mW per Li-ion Tamer sensor), no component prices were found, automatic charger cut-off adds mains-switching LVD scope, and insurers may expect UL 2075-type recognition.
justifications.c9: No evidence any insurer requests, accepts or discounts a charging log, and no comparable subscription pricing; only a competitor's vendor framing of 'supporting compliance'.
justifications.c10: Fire-service data (LFB), insurer loss data (Zurich, Aviva, AXA), trade press (Insurance Business, Post, BikeBiz, road.cc) and a first-hand forum thread (pedelecs.co.uk), though mostly about homes and retailers rather than hubs.

weakest: There is no identifiable, financially stable buyer: hub operators are small and have gone into administration, large operators ban on-site charging, and no insurer condition or log requirement creates a reason to pay.
